$ edit testdata/script/twice.txtar  # a variant with no about, states and lines nothing declares, and sections no registry claims
$ go test  # variants
    testdata/script/twice.txtar: variant/blank/about: the variant has no description: its about section is missing or empty
        Write each variant's description, in prose, in its about section.
    testdata/script/twice.txtar: gaps, line 1, names transform/nope, and no corpus type of testdata/script/ lists a transform of that name.
        List the transform, or remove the line.
    testdata/script/twice.txtar: variant/more/properties states loopy, and no registry under the module-root corpus lists a property of that name.
        Declare the property, or correct the line.
    testdata/script/twice.txtar: variant/more/gaps, line 1, names format, and no registry has a column of that name over the corpus script.
        Register the column, or remove the line.
    testdata/script/twice.txtar: no registry claims variant/more/out/shout/values.txt: no column named shout runs over the corpus script.
        If a column should write them, register the column. If not, run hypercase strip -column shout at the module root, then FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./... until it changes nothing. The strip removes shout's sections from every archive under the module-root corpus, and the update writes back each one a registry claims, but not one whose cell the update writes nothing for, such as a cell that faults.
    testdata/script/twice.txtar: no registry claims transform/nope/in/do/out/values.txt and transform/nope/out/echo/values.txt: no corpus type of testdata/script/ lists a transform named nope.
        If a transform should make the variant, list it in its corpus type's Transforms. If not, remove gaps line 1, which marks a cell of theirs, so that strip removes them; then run hypercase strip -transform nope at the module root, then FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./... until it changes nothing. The strip removes the sections under transform/nope/ from every archive under the module-root corpus, and the update writes back each one a registry claims, but not one whose cell the update writes nothing for, such as a cell that faults.
